notes: Commercial building lease dispute (barroom/restaurant/boarding-house uses, liquor prohibition, fire damage, partnership liability); boarding-house use mentioned only in passing as one of several tenant uses, not adjudicated.
Community-property/estoppel dispute over a plantation sale-with-lease-option contract; no lodging or room-letting issue.

Simms leased a building and operated it 'as a cheap hotel or rooming house,' but the litigation concerns his eviction as lessee, an alleged conspiracy, and a fire-marshal demolition order -- the legal character of the lodging business itself is not adjudicated.
Church-property trespass/ownership dispute among trustees; no lodging issue.

Homestead-exemption case for a widow supporting her adult daughters; a boarding-house-keeping widow appears only in a distinguished citation (Whyte v. Grant), a different case's facts, not Mrs. Gow's.
Zoning-nuisance injunction against a grocery store operating in a residential district; no lodging/boarding issue.
Stock/no-fence-law election dispute; no lodging issue.
Zoning-nuisance injunction against a drug store operating in a residential district; no lodging/boarding issue.
Taxpayer injunction suit over levee-board construction-zone sequencing on a lakefront reclamation project; no lodging issue.
Ejectment appeal dismissed on procedural/jurisdictional grounds (wrong appeal bond, amount not shown); no lodging issue reached.

holding_summary: Plaintiffs' family sub-let and occupied a room in a house owned by defendant, and their child was injured falling through an unfastened window screen; the appellate court affirmed judgment for the owner-defendant, holding that under Civil Code article 2716 the duty to fasten and maintain window screens falls on the tenant/occupant, not the owner.

quotes.text: Mrs. Sledge sublet a part of the leased premises, which included the room in which the window in question was located, to the plaintiffs
Mrs. Sledge sublet a part of the leased premises, which included the room in which the window in question was located, to the plaintiffs
It was the duty of the plaintiffs to have placed a hook on the screen and not the duty of the defendants, owners

notes: A tenant (Mrs. Sledge) sub-letting part of a dwelling to another family for rent is treated as an unremarkable, enforceable ordinary lease relationship, governed by standard landlord-tenant repair-duty rules; no explicit duration of the sub-tenancy is stated in the facts, so duration_of_occupancy is left unclear.
Agricultural land lease/provisional-seizure dispute over crop rent; no lodging/dwelling issue.
Farm-lease ejectment dispute over fence/terrace upkeep and appellate jurisdiction; no lodging issue.

A prospective purchaser under a failed agreement of sale took possession of the whole property and owes occupancy rent; this is an ordinary occupancy-pending-sale dispute, not a householder/commercial letting of rooms or a lodging/boarding arrangement.

Automobile-accident tort suit; the mother's rooming house is mentioned only in passing to compute her lost rental income ($5/week per room) as an element of damages, not to adjudicate any lodging issue.

Dispute between a landlord's statutory lien and a prior chattel mortgage on furniture in a building leased for a boarding-house business; addresses lien-priority ranking under the chattel mortgage act, not the legal character or regulation of the boarding-house occupancy itself.

holding_summary: An individual landlord who leased four rooms in a dwelling house to a tenant family at $40/month obtained a writ of provisional seizure over the tenant's furniture after the tenant fell behind on rent and began removing property; the court held the tenant's indebtedness and removal of furniture from the leased premises afforded ground for the writ, and affirmed judgment for the landlord.

quotes.text: In February, 1922, defendant, Grady C. Wheeler, leased from plaintiff- four; rooms in á dwelling house • in Shreveport at a monthly rental of $40.00.
In February, 1922, defendant, Grady C. Wheeler, leased from plaintiff- four; rooms in á dwelling house • in Shreveport at a monthly rental of $40.00.
The fact that he was indebted to plaintiff for rent and that he removed part of his furniture from the leased premises afforded ground for the writ of provisional seizure.

notes: An individual householder-landlord letting rooms in her own dwelling house to a family for monthly rent is treated as an ordinary, fully enforceable lease (rent recoverable, landlord's lien enforceable by provisional seizure), a favorable ordinary-incident-of-ownership pattern.
Possessory action over land and a ginhouse; no lodging issue.
